lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Coastal Marine Services | Diesel Mechanic | Lake City, USA | Jul 2025 - Present
- Rebuilt diesel engines and gearboxes for a fleet of 14 commercial fishing vessels, keeping dry-dock time under 5 days per job.
- Maintained hydraulic winch systems and logged service records for the harbor authority's annual inspections.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Rebuilt weekly carrier scorecards used by 6 regional managers to renegotiate contracts, cutting late deliveries from 11% to 7% in two quarters.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites; my redesign of the slotting rules was rolled out with the floor supervisors and 45 retrained pickers.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.

- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots while rewriting the standard operating procedures, running driver training and taking over vendor negotiations for the telematics contract, which saved 1,800 driver hours a year across the region.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
- Lifted checkout conversion from 61% to 66% by testing a one-page flow against the three-step flow across 40,000 sessions, then shipping it to all merchants.
- Prioritized the dispute roadmap with RICE, scoring Reach as the number of support tickets each feature would close.
- After interviewing 25 merchants, mapping chargeback reasons, sizing the loss by segment and drafting a business case with finance, set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran the checkout A/B test with randomization by session and reported the 5-point conversion lift as the effect on merchants' customers.
- Presented the onboarding results and a follow-up roadmap to the payments leadership team, who funded the rollout to two more regions.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Raised weekly active users from 400 to 1,150, a 150% increase, by adding pickup reminders chosen after 60 user interviews.
- Raised the pickup-slot fill rate by 20% across two dining halls, from 75% to 95%, by setting up a volunteer shift system.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Sized a $2.4M annual saving from consolidating outpatient scheduling across 4 clinics; the client funded a pilot based on the model.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Presented the final recommendation to the hospital COO and clinic directors, who approved a 90-day scheduling pilot at two clinics.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Reorder Experience by date so Harbor Payments appears before Crestline Logistics.
items.because: The current order makes the chronology harder to follow.

items.says: Add a short positioning section or headline that makes the intended PM role and career path clear.
items.because: The product evidence is dispersed across roles, and the current job title points in a different direction.

items.says: Replace the contact details if the phone number and example.com addresses are literal placeholders.
items.because: They look nonfunctional and would undermine the application.

items.says: Explain the move into the current Diesel Mechanic role for PM applications.
items.because: The rest of the résumé points toward product management, leaving readers to infer the career transition.

items.says: Clarify what “under 5 days per job” measures.
items.because: The turnaround measure could be ambiguous.

items.says: Clarify the scale, responsibility, or consequence of the hydraulic-systems work, or reconsider its space.
items.because: This bullet is less distinctive and may not earn space on a product-focused résumé.

items.says: Clarify the timeframe and comparison behind the 11% and 7% late-delivery figures.
items.because: Readers need to understand how the figures were measured.

items.says: Remove the switch to first person in “my redesign.”
items.because: The rest of the résumé generally does not use first person.

items.says: Check that “forecast error” has a consistent definition.
Prioritize the most relevant contribution and outcome in the route-planning bullet.
items.because: The rollout, SOP work, training, negotiations, and savings compete for attention and make the result harder to absorb.

items.says: Make your personal role in the reported driver-hour savings clear.
Clarify how “time to first payment” was measured.
Clarify whether the time reduction applies to the pilot population.
Specify whether the 61% to 66% conversion change was the A/B test result or a post-launch result.
items.because: The distinction matters when presenting an experiment’s impact.

items.says: Distinguish the RICE bullet from the following roadmap-prioritization bullet.
items.because: Both describe roadmap prioritization without clearly adding separate evidence.

items.says: Verify that the description of how Reach was defined and scored is accurate.
items.because: The current detail may prompt questions about the method.

items.says: Clarify what the merchant research and business case contributed beyond the RICE bullet.
items.because: The two bullets overlap in their roadmap-prioritization story.

items.says: Clarify whether the resulting roadmap priority was approved or implemented.
Remove the A/B-test bullet or make its experiment-design or analysis evidence distinct.
items.because: It repeats the conversion test and lift already described above.

items.says: Clarify what “effect on merchants’ customers” means.
items.because: The reported effect’s meaning is unclear.

items.says: Distinguish presenting the onboarding results, securing funding, and what had launched by the internship’s end.
Be ready to substantiate how the food-redistribution total was counted.
The increase from 400 to 1,150 weekly active users is 187.5%, not 150%.
items.because: The discrepancy is a visible credibility issue.

items.says: Clarify the measurement period and what “weekly active” means.
The change from 75% to 95% is 20 percentage points, not 20%.
items.because: The stated unit is incorrect.

items.says: Distinguish the modeled annual savings opportunity from savings actually realized.
items.because: Client funding is evidence of impact, not proof that the full estimate was achieved.

items.says: Replace the passive phrasing and say what you personally contributed.
items.because: The bullet is the vaguest in the résumé.

items.says: Give a measure of the intake changes’ scope or result, or remove the bullet.
items.because: It currently gives no such measure.

items.says: Distinguish this pilot-approval outcome from the preceding bullet’s pilot-funding outcome, or keep only one.
items.because: The two bullets overlap.

items.says: Make sure the broad product-skills list reflects capabilities substantiated in the experience bullets.
Consider adding important PM methods you actually use if the list omits them.
items.because: The skills list is broad.

items.says: Consider adding other tools only if you have practical experience with them.
items.because: The tools list is a useful but brief start.
